body:
Founder real-time: "continue tyler series x" -> "you know i hate calls" -> (mid-draft) "hold" ->
"ok continue". Published Series X x07, "The Editorial Meeting" -- direct follow-up to x06, next
morning, same crew.

First Series X interlude built with zero live gpt2-alpine-c calls. Every prior entry (x01-x06)
ran a real 5-call render ramp (16/32/64/128/256 tokens, ~11 min); this one runs none, and that
absence is the episode's own actual plot: the crew decides, on camera, to stop auto-chaining
render seeds from one episode's own unvetted output into the next episode's seed -- closing both
of x06's own explicitly-flagged open threads (does the fabrication problem escalate, should
seeding keep chaining) without pretending to know which explanation for x06's own content was
correct.

A real, honest mirror of the actual founder feedback that shaped it ("you know i hate calls"),
stated as such in the production note rather than invented to fill space -- "television as code"
applied literally: the real methodology changed mid-session, so the show's own in-universe
methodology changed with it, same episode.

TYLER commits f2e3b0a/6294b8a.
